Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and the base of G4591; unmarked, i.e. (figuratively) ignoble:--mean.
BiblicalUsage: This word is used once, when Paul is seized in Jerusalem and asks to speak. He says, I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city, and he asks leave to speak unto the people.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for a city of no mean standing carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the moment, that Paul claims his citizenship before he claims his gospel, and the captain lets him speak.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
